title: PATRICIA-3: A study of a chemotherapy-free combination of therapies (including zongertinib) for people with advanced ER-positive/HER2-positive breast cancer.
official: A phase Ib/II of chemotherapy-free trial evaluating Zongertinib in combination with Ribociclib, Endocrine Therapy and Trastuzumab in patients with ER-positive/HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer - PATRICIA-3 -
summary:
Main objective: phase Ib: To determine the maximum tolerated dose (MTD) and the recommended Phase II dose (RP2D) of ribociclib when administered in combination with zongertinib, trastuzumab and ET in patients with ER+/HER2+ advanced BC.
phase II: To evaluate the anti-tumor activity of zongertinib  in combination with  ribociclib, trastuzumab, and ET in patients with ER+/HER2+ ABC.
conditions: Patients with metastatic ER-positive/HER2-positive BC who have previously received at least one line of HER2-targeted therapy for advanced disease, including prior treatment with Trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd).
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Male or female patients ≥ 18 years of age at the time of signing the Informed Consent Form.
2. Baseline LVEF ≥50% measured using echocardiogram or equilibrium isotopic ventriculography (MUGA).
3. Participants with a history of treated CNS metastases are eligible, provided they meet all the following criteria: Evaluable disease outside the CNS is present; no evidence of interim CNS progression between the completion of CNSdirected therapy and the screening radiographic study; no  stereotactic radiation within 7 days or whole-brain radiation  within 14 days prior to study treatment initiation.
4. If female, patients must be postmenopausal or premenopausal with estradiol levels within postmenopausal range.
5. Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 0 or 1.
6. Advanced breast cancer (not amenable to curative therapy) histologically confirmed ER+/HER2+ breast cancer confirmed by local laboratory testing. ER positivity is defined as ≥10% of cells expressing ER via IHC analysis. HER2 positive tumor defined as either IHC 3+ or in situ hybridization positive (ISH+).
7. Able to provide a new formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tumor sample (preferred) or archived tumor tissue (most recent sample available from metastatic setting).
8. Has received prior treatment with T-DXd. Patients with recurrent disease in the first 12 months after finalizing adjuvant treatment with T-DXd will also be eligible.
9. Previous treatment with CDK4/6 inhibitors, TKI and endocrine therapy in any setting is permitted.
10. Have adequate organ function.
11. Measurable or evaluable disease.
12. QTcF interval (QT interval using Fridericia’s correction) at screening < 470 msec (females) or <450msec (males)
Exclusion criteria:
1. Prior therapy with ribociclib (except in cases where ribociclib was given for ≤21 days and was discontinued for reasons other than progression or severe toxicity).
2. Clinically significant, uncontrolled heart disease and/or cardiac repolarization abnormality, including uncorrected dyselectrolytemias or concomitant medication(s) with a known risk to prolong the QT interval and/or known to cause TdP that cannot be discontinued or replaced by safe alternative medication (e.g. within 5 half-lives or 7 days prior to starting trial treatment).
3. Uncontrolled arterial hypertension with systolic blood pressure > 180 mmHg or hypotension <90 mmHg.
4. History of LVEF decrease to <40% or symptomatic congestive heart failure during prior treatment with trastuzumab.
5. Concurrent treatment with strong or moderate cytochrome P450 (CYP)3A4/5 inhibitors or inducers, BCRP substrates or CYP2C8 substrates narrow therapeutic index.
6. History of non-infectious ILD/pneumonitis that has required steroids, or current ILD/pneumonitis (any grade).
7. Refractory nausea and vomiting, malabsorption syndrome, chronic gastrointestinal disease, inability to swallow the formulated product or previous significant bowel resection, or other condition that would preclude adequate absorption of any of the study drugs (e.g. Crohn’s disease, ulcerative colitis, chronic diarrhea).
